instructions: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in a pot with 1 3/4 cups water and cover.
Bring the rice to a boil over high heat, about 4 minutes. Turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid. Take it off the heat and let it sit, covered, for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, pull the crab sticks apart into thin strands, using 6 oz. Thinly slice the green onions.
Beat the eggs in a large bowl with the salt. Stir in the crab and green onions.
In a small pot, stir 1 1/3 cups water, the bouillon powder, the soy sauce, the sugar and the vinegar over medium heat until the sugar dissolves.
Stir the cornstarch with 2 tbsp water in a cup. Bring the sauce to a simmer, pour in the cornstarch mixture and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until it's thick and clear. Take it off the heat.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a splash of soy sauce.
Fluff the rice and divide it among 4 wide bowls.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Pour in a quarter of the egg mixture. Stir gently for 30 seconds, until the edges are set and the top is still soft and wet. Stop there. A dry omelet won't take up the sauce.
Slide the omelet onto a bowl of rice so it covers the rice.
Cook the other 3 omelets the same way, 1 tbsp oil each and about 1 minute apiece, sliding each onto a bowl of rice.
Warm the sauce for 30 seconds if it has cooled. Spoon a quarter of the sauce over each omelet.
method_notes: The lead (RecipeTinEats, 5 stars from 3 ratings, the trusted-cook fallback) makes a soft crab omelet, slides it onto rice and pours a thickened sweet and sour sauce over it. Japanese Taste uses the same layout with oyster sauce, mirin and a sprinkle of sesame oil. This uses the lead's Tokyo-style sauce with vinegar, multiplied for four and made without butter. The rice is the long part, so it's 33 minutes in all, a little over the 30-minute target.
